paragraphs: Rabbi Yose bar Assi: Mekhilta, Yitro, parashah BaChodesh, chapter 3.
Rabbi Yaakov bar Assi: Yelamdenu, beginning of Pekudei.

notes.text: The William Davidson digital text of Eruvin 59b fully writes Rav Chiyya bar Assi. This supports Rav for the first notice’s abbreviated ר׳; the other notices remain separate.

The consulted Tanchuma, Pekudei 2, explicitly names Rabbi Yaakov berabbi Assi in the homily comparing the Tabernacle with creation; its English translation spells the father Issi. This provides a named parallel to Hyman’s Yelamdenu reference near the beginning of Pekudei, without claiming inspection of his exact Yelamdenu printing. For the second notice, the Vilna 1884-labeled digital Notes and Corrections on Lekach Tov, Exodus 24:9, explicitly quotes Mekhilta, Yitro, chapter 3, with Rabbi Yose berabbi Assi. The same textual note records Rabbi Yishmael berabbi Yose in Yalkut and Rabbi Yose berabbi Yehudah in its base text; the consulted Beeri Mekhilta 3:3 likewise reads Yose berabbi Yehudah. The exact Mekhilta editions behind these readings have not been independently collated. These three patronymic notices do not establish that their fathers were one person.
